subject: Intermittent 504s impacting lyric-lite-2b — escalation & mitigation
messages:
From: Elliot Rogers <elliot@lyric.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Greer <sofia@lyric.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Elevated 504s while calling lyric-lite-2b generate

Hi Kim / Redwood,

We started seeing an uptick in 504 Gateway Timeout responses around 09:05 PST when calling the /v1/generate endpoint against model 'lyric-lite-2b'. Rough numbers: ~8% of requests are returning 504s; errors spike when we send longer prompts (>1.5k tokens) and when concurrency hits ~35 reqs/s. Affected request IDs (sample): req_9a8c2, req_9a8c5, req_9a8f1.

Attached are a small set of request logs and a screenshot of error rate. Can you confirm if this is a cluster-level issue or model-specific degradation? Our production flows are impacted (some customers report timeouts). We’re ready to move to a fallback model if you recommend one.

Thanks,
Elliot Rogers
Head of Platform — Lyric AI
elliot@lyric.ai

Attachment: lyric_request_log_20261212.csv (csv)
Attachment: runtime-traces-lyric-12-12.png (png)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elliot Rogers <elliot@lyric.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-12T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s while calling lyric-lite-2b generate

Thanks for flagging this, Elliot — we’ve received the logs and have opened an ops incident (LYR-0421).

Quick notes:
- Acknowledged: we see a correlated increase in 504s in telemetry for lyric-lite-2b around 09:03–09:18 PST.
- Short-term mitigation: if you can route traffic to lyric-base-1.3 (compatible API surface) we expect markedly fewer timeouts; alternatively reduce concurrency to <=20 reqs/s for the next 2h while we triage.
- Action: infra is triaging kernel selection and KV-cache behavior, and engineering is rolling a targeted change to request batching logic.

I’ll keep you updated with concrete ETA for the fix. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your customers.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elliot Rogers <elliot@lyric.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s while calling lyric-lite-2b generate

Status update (ops):

- Triage summary: root cause appears to be a regression in kernel selection for lyric-lite-2b under mixed-sequence workloads. Under certain prompt distributions the runtime is choosing a fallback kernel path that bypasses the optimized KV cache hot path, increasing tail latency and triggering head-of-line 504s.
- Impact window: observed 09:03–10:45 PST with residual elevated latency through ~11:00.
- Mitigation applied: pushed a targeted kernel-selection patch (patch-lyric-lite-20261212.diff) to affected nodes and temporarily lowered batch size thresholds for lyric-lite-2b. Early telemetry shows errors drop to <0.5% within 25 minutes after the patch.
- Customer-facing ask: If Lyric can retain traffic on lyric-base-1.3 for 2–4 hours we will perform a controlled verification sweep before rolling fully back.

We will produce a postmortem and a follow-up notice describing the kernel selector fix and recommended client-side fallbacks (max_concurrency, max_tokens).

—Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-12-14T16:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s while calling lyric-lite-2b generate — incident closed & next steps

Hi Elliot / Sofia,

Thanks again for your patience. Final update and next steps from Redwood for incident LYR-0421:

What we changed:
- Deployed a kernel-selection patch to all lyric-lite-2b serving nodes (rolled out 12/12 11:10 PST, verified 12/12 11:35 PST).
- Tuned batching thresholds and reduced default max_batch_size for lyric-lite-2b for 72 hours to avoid regression while we stabilize.
- Added extra telemetry on sequence-length distribution to the alerting predicate.

Outcome:
- Error rate returned to baseline (~0.2% tail errors) within 25–30 minutes of the patch. No further customer-facing timeouts reported after 12/12 11:40 PST.

Postmortem / follow-ups:
- Draft postmortem: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/LYR-0421 (internal view). We’ll share a redacted customer-friendly summary by 2026-12-16.
- Action items: engineering will ship a permanent kernel selector fix in the next minor release (v1.8.3) and a safer default batching config. Ops will keep the temporary batching config for 72 hours and then step down once telemetry is stable.
- Credits: Ben — we’ve applied a modest service credit against December usage for Lyric AI; Kim will follow up with the exact credit amount and the adjusted invoice.

If it’s OK, we’d like to schedule a 30-min sync (this week) to walk through the postmortem and confirm client-side mitigations. Would 09:30 PST on Friday (12/17) work for you?

Apologies again for the interruption and thanks for the quick examples — they were instrumental in reducing time to remediation.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
